facts.value: A void-returning GObj user-data destructor callback with source-level signature void(void*); its argument is expected to point to an ItemLink record allocated from item_link_alloc_data. It returns normally after recycling the record.
facts.rationale: Replace ambiguous no-return terminology with the actual void-returning signature and preserve the constructor-proven payload contract.

evidence.why: Exact wrapper signature and body.
Pool allocation and destructor registration establish the payload contract.
The free operation returns normally.

facts.value: Uses the next link's collision position as the sweep origin when that link exists and has x2C_b0 set; otherwise uses its own previous collision position. If that next link has contact while the current link does not, an island lookup and either coordinate test can set link.pos.y to island.x14.y and return the existing masked environment flags before collision resolution, contact refresh, audio, or final position writeback. Otherwise prior x2C_b1 selects the collision routine. Floor flags restore the proposed X coordinate; absent floor flags, wall flags add the supplied Y offset when the next link is active, prev is non-null, and the next link is lower. A false-to-true x2C_b1 transition with x2C_b2 clear calls the character-dependent audio routine and sets x2C_b2. This function never clears that latch.
facts.rationale: Replaces lifetime-wide and neighbor-activity assumptions with the exact current guards and explicitly distinguishes the early-return path from normal collision processing.

evidence.why: Complete body establishes the history preparation, shortcut returns, collision guards, audio latch and copyback.

facts.value: Receives an ItemLink starting node, a fighter-side caller's matrix-derived target, article special attributes and the owning Fighter. The inspected caller supplies linkhookshot.x0, the prev-null endpoint stored as constructor last_link. The helper reads motion-dependent thresholds and spacing x30, writes successor positions, activation flags and collision-position history, and forwards the final visited link and target to it_802A49B0. Its boolean selects either an attachment-relative matrix update for the x0 endpoint or synchronization of segment JObjs from existing link positions, using the target as a boundary and fighter Y scale as uniform model scale.
facts.rationale: Preserves the supported data flow and false-path segment-model correction while replacing ambiguous first-link terminology with the constructor-proven x0 endpoint identity.

evidence.why: Defines helper inputs, thresholds and mutations.
Defines segment-model synchronization.
Caller supplies x0 and selects the two transform paths.
Constructor last_link has prev == NULL.
Stores last_link in x0 and first_link in x4.

facts.value: Returns true without processing links when motions 0xD4, 0xD6 or 0x168 have mv.ca.specials.grav below ext-attribute x88, x98 or xA8 respectively. Otherwise it traverses successors, clamps active links to maximum spacing x30 and advances collision history. An inactive successor is activated one x30 interval toward the target only when the target distance exceeds x30; otherwise it returns false. Chain exhaustion calls it_802A49B0 and returns false. The inspected caller maps true to an attachment-relative matrix update of the x0/prev-null endpoint, constructor last_link, and false to segment-JObj synchronization.
facts.rationale: Preserves the supported threshold and link-state behavior, corrects the false-path output, and makes endpoint terminology explicit.

evidence.why: Contains all guards, mutations and returns.
Shows the false-path effects.
Shows x0 matrix handling and return-value routing.
Constructor last_link is prev-null.
Binds that endpoint to x0.

facts.value: Consumes a JObj, position and mutable direction. It normalizes direction in place and uses positive Y as its reference seed, except that direction.y > 0.9999 selects negative X and direction.y < -0.9999 selects positive X. Two cross products and normalization construct the remaining basis columns. Direction becomes column 2, position becomes translation column 3, and the completed matrix, flags 0x03800000 and dirty state are published to the JObj.
facts.rationale: Corrects the reference-axis description while retaining the directly observed matrix data flow.

evidence.why: Explicit seed branches, basis assignments and JObj writes.

facts.value: Reads the stored x4 chain endpoint, link activity and positions, neighboring positions, caller boundary, owner facing and model scale. After skipping inactive links from x4, it traverses prev links. For each visited link with prev != NULL it writes JObj translation and computes direction as prev_pos minus next_pos, substituting the caller boundary when the successor is absent or inactive, then forwards position, direction and scale to it_802A6F80. The prev-null endpoint instead receives direction (1,0,0) when owner facing_dir is positive and (-1,0,0) otherwise. On the constructed chain that facing-only endpoint is x0, constructor last_link; constructor first_link is the next-null endpoint stored in x4.
facts.rationale: Preserves the direction-polarity correction and exact facing condition while repairing the inconsistent first/last endpoint terminology.

evidence.why: Defines traversal, subtraction and separate prev-null facing-end handling.
Shows downstream position, direction and scale consumption.
Distinguishes next-null first_link from prev-null last_link.
Stores those endpoints in x4 and x0 respectively.

facts.value: Reads Fighter userdata from the incoming HSD_GObj and reads fp->u.lk.xC. If non-null, passes that tracked Item GObj unchanged to it_802A2B10 and returns. The callee follows linkhookshot.x8, not Item.owner, and clears x10, the retained fighter's tracked article and three callbacks, destroys linked segment GObjs, and removes the item only when item userdata, x8, and retained Fighter userdata are valid. If fp->u.lk.xC is null, this entry point directly clears accessory2_cb, death1_cb, and accessory3_cb.
facts.rationale: Corrects the referenced field and preserves the callee's explicit nested guards.

evidence.why: Complete caller data flow.
Complete callee guards, retained-reference lookup, writes and destruction.

facts.value: Fighter-side Hookshot cleanup entry point: requests guarded teardown of the fighter's tracked article when present, or directly unregisters three fighter callbacks when no article is tracked.
facts.rationale: Describes the demonstrated cleanup request without promising destruction when the callee's retained-reference guards fail.

evidence.why: Selects delegation or direct callback clearing.
Delegated teardown is conditional.

facts.value: With no tracked article, clears accessory2_cb, death1_cb, and accessory3_cb directly. With a tracked article, delegates to it_802A2B10 and returns without fallback. Successful delegated cleanup clears the retained fighter's article pointer and callbacks and destroys the chain and item; if item userdata, linkhookshot.x8, or retained Fighter userdata is null, delegated cleanup has no effects. This entry point performs no timer update or item motion-state transition.
facts.rationale: Replaces unconditional path convergence with the actual guarded behavior, including the independently clearable x8 reference.

evidence.why: Immediate return after delegation and null-article callback branch.
All state-changing effects are nested inside validity guards.
Reference invalidation can clear x8 independently.
